title: OR-1 phase 1: independent-brainstorm primitive (product, not meta)
plan: OR-1 (owner_requests.json, value 95, top of backlog) needs a 4-phase debate where phase 1 is agents drafting COMPLETELY ALONE, no cross-talk. The existing room engine (src/excava_chat.py advance()) only does sequential shared-history debate -- it cannot express phase 1 at all. Built or1_phase1(element_type) + CLI --or1-phase1: each 'improve' agent gets an isolated engines.complete() call (no _history()), hard-gated on >=2 LIVE distinct model families (END PLAN section 2 bans same-model-with-a-persona-twist as correlated-error theater). Ran for element_type=skill: correctly BLOCKED (this cloud session only carries a GitHub-Models key -> 1 live family, GPT-4o-mini) and wrote an honest artifact (data/excava/artifacts/or1-phase1-skill.md) instead of faking a multi-agent debate with one model. CARRY-OVER for the next fire(s) with real provider-key access (the GitHub Actions beat carries the full secret set per SESSION_HANDOFF.md): run --or1-phase1 for each of the 10 element/package types, confirm >=2 families actually respond, then build phase 2 (integration discussion), phase 3 (adversarial re-review from scratch), phase 4 (resolution) on the same isolated-call pattern before wiring the final committed guideline artifact OR-1 promises.

notes.text: Fire 3 on this increment (cloud, scheduled/away-mode invocation). Re-confirmed the block is unchanged: this session still carries no provider key beyond GH_TOKEN (no GEMINI_API_KEY/GROQ/etc in env) -- families() still reports 1 live lineage, so a real --or1-phase1 sweep of the 10 element types is still not possible from here. Rather than re-running the same blocked call a third time or padding with unrelated meta-work, built the next REAL piece the carry-over plan named: or1_phase2() (integration discussion) in src/excava_chat.py + CLI --or1-phase2, on the identical isolated-call pattern as phase 1 (no _history(), hard-gated on >=2 live families, refuses to run without a successful phase-1 artifact for the same element type -- phase 2 has nothing to integrate otherwise). Also generalized _write_or1_artifact to write a JSON sidecar alongside the markdown (phase 2 needs phase 1's raw drafts back, not just prose) -- non-breaking, phase 1's existing filename/behavior unchanged. New src/or1_phase_test.py (16 checks, stdlib-only, no network, mocks src.excava_engines + src.excava_agents) proves: the family-count gate blocks BEFORE making any engine call (both phases), phase 2 refuses without a phase-1 artifact, phase 1's isolated calls carry zero cross-agent leakage, phase 2's integration prompts are correctly seeded with EVERY phase-1 draft, and phase 2's own calls are isolated from each other too (phase 2 is a second solo pass, not a debate -- letting phase-2 responses see each other would just move phase 1's anchoring problem one step later). Ran `python -m src.or1_phase_test`: 16/16 pass. Ran `python -m src.excava_chat --or1-phase2 skill` for real against this session's actual (keyless) engines: correctly BLOCKED, wrote data/excava/artifacts/or1-phase2-skill.{md,json} -- same honest-blocked-artifact pattern as phase 1, not a faked debate. `python -m src.excava_core_test`: still all pass (untouched). CARRY-OVER UNCHANGED for the next fire with real keys: run --or1-phase1 across all 10 element/package types, then --or1-phase2 on each once phase 1 lands, then build phase 3 (adversarial re-review from scratch) and phase 4 (resolution) on this same pattern before wiring the final committed guideline artifact OR-1 promises. Harsh self-criticism: this is still 0 LIVE multi-family runs after 3 fires -- the actual OR-1 deliverable (a real cross-model guideline) has not moved, only the machinery to produce it has. That machinery is now 2/4 phases built and unit-tested, which is real, verifiable progress, but Eitan should know the keyless-cloud-session limitation is structural, not something a 4th fire here will fix -- it needs the GH Actions beat (full secret set) or a session with provider keys to actually execute.

notes: verify_elements --limit 200 (next-highest backlog item, value 87) also aborted safely on this session's proxy-restricted egress -- same known limitation as fire 50, no data written, nothing to fix.
build_memory (value 64) needs GEMINI_API_KEY, also absent here -- confirms this interactive session is genuinely keyless beyond GitHub Models, not a bug to chase.

notes.text: SELF-CORRECTION on this fire's own previous note: the claim that discover_promote was 'never wired into any CI workflow, only runnable by hand' was WRONG -- caught before finalizing, not after. src/excava.py's beat() calls discover_promote.promote() directly, and bulk_analyze.yml runs 'python -m src.excava' every ~2-3h, which is what actually produced the 04:05Z/07:10Z/10:20Z updates to data/discovered_elements.json today (confirmed via git log --follow on that file). The only real, separate, already-known issue is guardrails G-P: the DEDICATED excava_beat.yml lane (every 10min) is stale (6.9h since last commit) -- not something this fire fixed. Kept the core_spoton.yml addition of a discover_promote step anyway, on the correct narrower justification: core_spoton.yml runs hourly and is currently healthy (G-Q, 1.7h), so it gives the Sources-tab output a second, more reliable path independent of the wedged excava_beat lane -- a real but smaller freshness win (~3h -> ~1h with redundancy) than first claimed. Lesson for next fire: verify a step is actually orphaned via 'git log --follow -- <output-file>' (who really writes it), not just grep of workflow YAML for the function name.

Harsh self-criticism: still 0 LIVE multi-family runs after 4 fires -- machinery is now 3/4 phases built and unit-tested (up from 2/4), which is real verifiable progress, but the actual OR-1 deliverable has not moved an inch, and this is structural (needs the GH Actions beat's full secret set or a keyed session), not something a 5th fire here fixes alone.

Fire 5 on this increment (cloud, scheduled/away-mode). Confirmed still keyless (only GH_TOKEN in env, families()==1 live lineage) -- a real multi-family sweep is still not possible from here. Built or1_phase4() (resolution discussion, the FINAL phase) in src/excava_chat.py + CLI --or1-phase4, completing all 4 phases the OR-1 spec names. Same isolated-call pattern as phases 2/3: no shared history, hard-gated on >=2 live families, and now a DOUBLE prerequisite (needs both phase-2's integrated set AND phase-3's weakness lists on disk for the element type -- phase 4 resolves phase 3's criticisms against phase 2's actual guideline text, not phase 3's output alone). Each agent's prompt is seeded with both corpora and asked to explicitly rule KEPT/FIXED/REJECTED on every weakness before writing the final GOOD/MEDIOCRE/DISQUALIFIED guideline as a finished ruling, not another draft -- this is the artifact done_criteria calls 'the final committed guideline set.' Extended src/or1_phase_test.py with 19 new checks (38 total, up from 27): phase4 blocks with no phase-3 artifact and separately with no phase-2 artifact (two distinct gates, both zero-engine-calls); phase4 also independently gates on family diversity; phase4 succeeds once both prereqs exist, one isolated call per cast member, every prompt seeded with ALL of phase-2's integration drafts AND ALL of phase-3's weakness lists; zero cross-agent leakage; both artifact files written. python -m src.or1_phase_test: 38/38 pass. python -m src.excava_chat --or1-phase4 skill for real against this session's actual keyless engines: correctly BLOCKED on the phase-3-artifact prerequisite (this session's own or1-phase3-skill.json is itself a blocked artifact) -- same honest-blocked-artifact pattern as phases 1-3, not a faked resolution. python -m src.excava_core_test: 28/28 pass (untouched). guardrails 17/20, 0 critical (same non-critical G-C/G-O/G-P as before -- G-C self-heals on ship, G-O/G-P are PC-drain/beat-lane staleness unrelated to this change). MACHINERY IS NOW COMPLETE: all 4 OR-1 phases exist, are unit-tested (38 checks), and chain correctly (phase N refuses without phase N-1's real artifact). The actual OR-1 deliverable -- a live cross-model guideline for even one element type -- still has NOT been produced, because this cloud session has never carried >=2 live provider-model families in 5 fires. CARRY-OVER for the next fire with real keys (the GitHub Actions beat carries the full secret set per SESSION_HANDOFF.md): run --or1-phase1 for each of the 10 element/package types, then --or1-phase2, --or1-phase3, --or1-phase4 per type in order -- the pipeline itself needs zero further engineering, only execution. Harsh self-criticism: 5 fires spent building a 4-phase pipeline and 0 fires spent producing what OR-1 actually asked for (a guideline). That ratio is defensible only because the primitive genuinely did not exist (advance()'s shared-history debate cannot express phase 1's no-cross-talk rule) and building it wrong once, then live is worse than building it once and testing it thoroughly -- but if the next fire with real keys ALSO can't execute this (e.g. a provider outage), that becomes a real problem, not a structural one, and should trigger reconsidering whether this session should request a provider key be added to the cloud secret set instead of waiting on the beat.

Fire 6 on this increment (cloud, scheduled/away-mode). Confirmed still keyless (only GH_TOKEN, families()==1 live lineage). Instead of a 6th blocked CLI call, traced WHY 5 fires of carry-over notes assumed the GitHub Actions beat would eventually execute this and never did: grep of every .github/workflows/*.yml for or1_phase/excava_chat found ZERO references -- the pipeline was fully built and unit-tested but never called from any scheduled workflow, keyed or not. That was the real blocker, not missing keys. Fixed it directly: added or1_next_phase(element_type) (first phase in 1..4 without an ok:true artifact on disk) and or1_run_all(types) (sweeps all 10 types, advances each by exactly one phase, skips fully-resolved types) to src/excava_chat.py, plus --or1-run-all CLI flag. Wired a new step into .github/workflows/bulk_analyze.yml (2h cadence, already carries the full multi-provider secret set -- GEMINI x6/GROQ x2/CEREBRAS x2/MISTRAL/OPENROUTER/NVIDIA/SAMBANOVA -- the same pool engine_selftest proved live) calling 'python -m src.excava_chat --or1-run-all'. Extended src/or1_phase_test.py with 6 new checks (44 total, up from 38): or1_next_phase returns None once phase4 succeeded / 1 for an untouched type; run_all skips a fully-resolved type with zero engine calls; run_all advances a fresh type's phase 1 and writes its artifact; run_all degrades gracefully (BLOCKED, no crash) when every type is below the family gate. python -m src.or1_phase_test: 44/44 pass. python -m src.excava_core_test: 28/28 pass (untouched). Ran python -m src.excava_chat --or1-run-all for real against this session's actual keyless engines: all 10 types correctly BLOCKED at phase 1 (families()==1), zero crashes, zero fake artifacts -- and for the first time ALL 10 types now have an honest blocked artifact on record instead of just skill. Harsh self-criticism: this is still 0 LIVE multi-family runs -- the actual OR-1 deliverable (a real cross-model guideline) still has not been produced by ANY fire yet. But the nature of the block changed: it is no longer 'waiting on a decision only Eitan can make' (5 fires assumed that), it's 'waiting on the next bulk_analyze.yml run' (~2h, already scheduled, no action needed) -- a genuinely different and better state that didn't require asking Eitan for a new secret. If bulk_analyze.yml runs and OR-1 is STILL all-blocked next fire, that would mean the beat's own multi-provider pool doesn't actually clear the family gate either, which would be a real, non-structural problem worth surfacing directly. CARRY-OVER: watch data/excava/artifacts/or1-phase*.json after the next few bulk_analyze runs for the first ok:true phase-1 artifacts; once phase 1 lands for all 10 types the sweep will auto-advance them through 2/3/4 on subsequent runs with zero further engineering.
